neighbours.label: The word just before 'true' when a speaker affirms or denies a claim just made ("that's⟦ very⟧ true", "is simply⟦ not⟧ true"); weak
fire: My father used to say that haste makes waste, and that's very true.
The brochure says the hotel is near the beach, which is simply not true.
She told me the first year is the hardest, and that's very true in my case.
Some insist the old mill is haunted, but that is just not true.
You said good tools pay for themselves, and that's very true.
The rumour that the school will close is simply not true.
People claim the film follows the book closely, and that's very true for the first half.
He keeps telling everyone I quit, which is simply not true.
quiet: My father used to say that haste makes waste, and that's very old advice.
The brochure says the hotel is near the beach, which is simply not open in winter.
She told me the first year is the hardest, and that's very hard to hear.
Some insist the old mill is haunted, but that is just not my concern.
You said good tools pay for themselves, and they are very costly.
The path that leads to the school is simply not safe.
People claim the film follows the book closely, and it's very long in the first half.
He keeps telling everyone I quit, which is simply not kind.

notes: Card: no single token; top 'made a⟦ good⟧ point', 'that's⟦ very⟧ true', 'Isn⟦'t⟧ True', plus ' B' after Stephen/Steven (the opposite pole fires on 'I⟦ was⟧ right/wrong'). Probes: 'that's very true' 0.45, 'simply not true' 0.35, 'made a good point' 0.22, 'isn't true' 0.20; 'so true' 0.09, 'absolutely true' 0.05, 'Stephen Baker' 0.03, 'it's very expensive' 0.02. Weak and partial.
